title: Nearly one in three homes was rented
description: Each square is about 1% of 9.3 million occupied homes. Renters (30.6%) nearly match outright owners (31.0%).

title: The separate house still defines the landscape
description: Box area shows how many homes of each type there were. Seven in ten are separate houses. Apartments, the most-rented type, are about 1 in 7 homes. Caravans and other homes (under 1%) are left out.

title: 63% of apartments are rented, against 21% of houses
description: Column width shows each type’s share of homes; colour shows how they are held. Renting sits on the baseline for easy comparison. Other types (1%) are left out.

title: One in four people living alone has an apartment
description: Each band links a household type to its home; wider bands mean more households. Four in five families live in a house. The dark band is people living alone in apartments.

title: A national median hides local differences
description: Darker regions have higher median weekly rents. Manly ($720) costs nine times Arnhem Land ($80). City insets are enlarged, so use their 10 km bars. Outlines mark the three communities in chapter 3.

title: Rented homes crowd into the capital cities
description: Dots sit in the small areas where renters live. Figure 05 showed price; this shows people. Most crowd into the capitals and the coast.
hint: Zoom with the buttons, ctrl + scroll or double-click; drag to move.

title: Most regions charge between $300 and $449
description: Each bar counts regions with a median rent in one $50 band. The dark bars are 194 of 335 regions, charging $300 to $449. Each region counts once.

title: There is no single rental market within a state
description: Each row is a state, sorted by its typical region. Lines run from the cheapest region to the dearest; boxes hold the middle half. NSW alone spans $150 to $720 a week.

title: Higher-income places often have higher rents
description: Each dot is a region; dashed lines mark the national medians. The grey line shows the overall trend. Melbourne City pays above-median rent on a below-median income. Click a featured dot to focus on it.

title: Similar rents can come with very different homes
description: Each line is a region, read across four measures. Melbourne City and Casey – South charge almost the same rent. Yet 86% of Melbourne City’s homes are apartments, against 1% in Casey – South. Hover any grey line to trace a region.

title: Rents are rising faster than prices overall
description: By July 2026 rents had risen 9.8% since April 2024. Prices across the economy rose 6.9%. Both are measured across the eight capital cities.

title: Assistance helps, but 44% stay in rental stress
description: Each pair is the same recipients in March 2026. Grey leaves rent assistance out; purple counts it. Rental stress means rent above 30% of income.

title: Students face the most rental stress in every state
description: Each cell is the share of recipients in rental stress after assistance; darker cells mean more stress. Students and apprentices top every state, at 74–87%.

title: 264,000 recipients pay over half their income in rent
description: Circle area shows how many recipients pay over half their income in rent, after assistance. Colour shows their share of the state’s recipients. NSW has the most; the ACT has the highest share.
